items: IoC (Inversion of Control) Container is the core of the Spring Framework.
It manages the lifecycle, configuration, and dependencies of application objects (beans).
Spring provides two types of IoC containers:
XML-Based Configuration involves defining beans and their dependencies in an external XML file.
This XML file is read by the Spring IoC Container to configure and manage beans.

rows: Root element; contains all bean definitions. Includes namespace declarations.
Declare XML namespaces and schema location for validation.
Used to define a bean that Spring will manage.
Unique name (identifier) used to retrieve the bean from the container.
Fully qualified class name of the Java object to be instantiated as a bean.
Spring IoC container; manages the bean lifecycle.
Loads XML configuration from the classpath.
Retrieves the bean instance using its id from XML config.
Typecast is needed since getBean() returns an Object.

items: Separation of concerns: Configuration is externalized from Java code.
Easy to manage: Multiple beans and their dependencies in a single XML.
Readability: Declarative approach makes dependencies clear.
No recompilation: You can update configurations without changing Java code.
Verbose: Tedious to manage as the project grows.
Harder to refactor: Changes in class/package require XML updates.
More error-prone: Typos or incorrect fully-qualified names lead to runtime errors.
